column1: # Shared instant-cache key vectors (#705). Read by ALL FOUR implementations of
# the Unix path -> cache-key encoder, so they cannot drift apart again:
# Format: one vector per line, tab-separated: input<TAB>expected.
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. Extra columns after
# `expected` are reserved for later issues (e.g. #771 long-key chunking) and
# MUST be ignored by readers that do not know them. Neither column may be
# empty (tab is IFS-whitespace to bash/zsh `read`, which would collapse it).
# `input` uses the same mini escape scheme as json_escape_vectors.tsv --
# backslash first: \\ -> one literal backslash byte, \n -> LF, \r -> CR,
# \t -> tab. `expected` is literal (the Unix key never contains a backslash,
# tab or newline) and is NOT unescaped.
# Unix scheme: exactly five escapes, `_` first: _->__ /->_s \->_b :->_c
# space->_w. Every other byte, including the Windows-reserved ? * < > " |,
# passes through unchanged. Every reader MUST fail if this file is missing or
